# Rakeback write authority — PostgreSQL qualification pending

The September 17 statistics-batch retirement and transition checks are **UNRUN**. Required qualification uses the restored original GitHub-hosted PostgreSQL 17 financial fixture job and its existing full-weekly runner. The formerly proposed protected local pipeline is retired. These files do not authorize a separate pipeline, production test activity or installation. Historical source-only statements below describe authored coverage, not an executed or installed result.

The 161000 component closes direct client table and column writes to `rakeback_periods` and `rakeback_period_payouts`. It preserves SELECT grants and RLS policies, retires the arbitrary JSON bulk-upsert body, revokes the dormant invoker factory's EXECUTE without changing its body, and leaves the existing service request wrapper and private postgres-owned writers in place. Effective inherited write rights cause the complete activation to refuse.

The bulk function is registered before replacement for the existing DDL gate, then marked `closed` after retirement so registry consumers do not count another approved writer. PostgreSQL 17 documents that table revokes also remove corresponding column grants; the explicit all-column revokes are additional checks, not a claim that table revokes never affect columns. Inherited grants still require the final effective-privilege check. See the primary [REVOKE documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-revoke.html) and [REINDEX privilege and transaction rules](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-reindex.html). Documentation review is not actual fixture execution.

## Installation transition boundary

Replacing the function and revoking EXECUTE prevents a **new** call after commit. It does not establish that a backend which already entered the old SECURITY DEFINER body cannot continue later; neither the existing period-table locks nor a proposed player-stats table lock prove all unstarted old-body writes have drained. The minimal prerequisite is the canonical-only engine precursor (no legacy stats/period calls), plus observed retirement/drain of every old engine process and its in-flight database work before activation. Retain exact deployed engine identity and original maintenance/drain/release evidence. A matching source hash, a quiet query snapshot or the fixture's after-commit refusal alone is not that proof. Do not install while old-writer work remains unknown, and do not add a background repair route. This task performs no engine or production database mutation.

The baseline table/column and function ACLs must remain bound to the captured evidence. The regression creates a transaction-local fixture schema with CREATE/USAGE for the three application roles, so a real ordinary-table foreign-key probe reaches the target table's REFERENCES check. PostgreSQL forbids a temporary table from referencing a permanent table, so a temporary-table probe would not qualify. The single fixture trigger function has no financial behavior and receives EXECUTE solely so the TRIGGER denial is for the protected table. No accounting table grants are added by the regression. All fixture additions are rolled back.

## What the authored regression exercises

- Real `SET LOCAL ROLE` calls for anon, authenticated and service_role; a real SELECT from both tables; real INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, TRUNCATE, REFERENCES, TRIGGER and REINDEX requests refused with SQLSTATE 42501 identifying the target table. REINDEX is the PostgreSQL 17 MAINTAIN probe; a warning-only ANALYZE would not qualify. Catalog checks additionally cover every effective table and column privilege.
- Three legacy APIs refuse at EXECUTE for all three roles: the period bulk writer, dormant period factory and player-statistics batch. The two former bulk writers also refuse accidental postgres calls with `rakeback_period_bulk_upsert_retired` and `rakeback_player_stats_batch_retired` (55000). The dormant factory's actual body remains unchanged. Together with the table probes, 51 real client calls must be denied.
- An actual service call enters the unchanged canonical request wrapper and actual mixed-source calculator. It creates one pending period plus its certificate and durable acknowledgment, updates the same period when a second source is supplied, and replays without a second certificate. Stored results and numeric values are checked; a blocked response is a failure, not successful execution.
- Full public/auth/cron rows, including statistics markers, player stats, periods, wallets and payout history, remain identical across all denied calls. The unchanged scalar stats helper is exercised as service_role once and on an exact-source duplicate with a differing payload; only the initial original source applies. No payout, chip journal, wallet balance change or paid period is produced.

The source is deliberately synthetic and in a future post-cutover week. The test owner constructs its raw attribution, immutable observed member contract and cash receipt-shaped rows; this does **not** prove source capture, bank recognition, the commercial rate model or financial eligibility. Fixture construction temporarily suppresses seed side effects; the canonical calls and permission probes run with actual triggers enabled. No production history or cutover is backdated, no historical period is reassigned, and no payer is called. A complete payment qualification still requires the existing actual routed-stage/central-invoice cases under protected execution; this limited fixture cannot establish payout correctness or production completion.

## Atomic rejection phases (parent-owned runner)

Preserve the existing 160000 fault phase. Add a separate disposable rejection phase after loading captured baseline ACLs: create a fixture-only role, grant it column UPDATE on `public.rakeback_periods(rakeback_amount)`, then grant that role to service_role with INHERIT TRUE. Snapshot the baseline schema/ACL and table rows after this intentional grant, apply the complete candidate with `ON_ERROR_STOP`, and require the stable error prefix `rakeback_write_authority_effective_column_privilege_remains:`. The component's direct table and column revokes cannot remove this inherited grant, so its final postcondition must refuse after attempting legacy bulk retirement, period ACL closure and cron retirement earlier in the bundle. Compare before/after schema, ACL and table-row digests in that same cluster; sequence gaps are not transactional row changes. Do not mark rollback proved merely because the expected exception appeared.

An independent preimage fault may instead append body whitespace to the captured bulk function before candidate execution. It must raise `rakeback_write_authority_function_preimage_changed: public.fn_rakeback_periods_bulk_upsert(jsonb)`. This earlier guard tests drift refusal but does not exercise the final inherited-right postcondition. Keep rejection and acceptance clusters independent and retain stopped-process and artifact receipts.

For a direct column-ACL revocation qualification, a separate acceptance fixture may add column INSERT/UPDATE/REFERENCES grants to each client and PUBLIC before candidate execution, preserving SELECT; verify the real denial probes after activation. This intentionally broader synthetic baseline must be labeled separately from the captured production ACL baseline. No such grant is made by `regression.sql` after activation.

The full activation builder/runner and source bindings are parent-owned. Required acceptance remains fresh protected source binding, actual parser/catalog/preimage execution, caller and canonical writer results, complete transaction rollback evidence, and separately authorized installation/live reconciliation.
